papers.title: Investigation of the properties of heat-resistant spherical powders
papers.abstract: Nowadays, additive manufacturing (AM) become very perspective method for fast fabrication of any details, parts or products. One of the main methods of AM is selective laser melting (SLM), which allows to obtain complex shape parts from various metal powders. However, this process requires high demands on the initial materials. To determine the quality of the initial EP648, EP741I, and Hastelloy X powders, such methods as scanning electron microscopy, laser diffraction, reductive melting and X-ray were used.

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the quality of EP648, EP741I, and Hastelloy X powders for selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: The powders were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, laser diffraction, reductive melting, and X-ray analysis.
summary_en.result: The morphology, particle size distribution, and chemical composition of the powders were determined.
summary_en.validation: Multiple characterization techniques were employed to cross-validate powder properties.

papers.title: Self-Contained Three-Dimensional Bioprinter for Applications in Cardiovascular Research
papers.abstract: Bioprinting is a technique of creating 3D cell-laden structures by accurately dispensing biomaterial to form complex synthetic tissue. The printed constructs aim to mimic the native tissue by preserving the cell functionality and viability within the printed structure. The 3D bioprinting system presented in this paper aims to facilitate the process of 3D bioprinting through its ability to control the environmental parameters within an enclosed printing chamber. This design of the bioprinter targets to eliminate the need for a laminar flow hood, by regulating the necessary environmental conditions important for cell survival, especially during long duration prints. A syringe-based extrusion (SBE) deposition method comprising multiple nozzles is integrated into the system. This allows for a wider selection of biomaterials that can be used for the formation of the extracellular matrix (ECM). Tissue constructs composed of alginate-gelatin hydrogels were mixed with fibrinogen and human endothelial cells which were then characterized and compared using two methodologies: casted and bioprinted. Furthermore, vasculature was incorporated in the bioprinted constructs using sacrificial printing. Structural and functional characterization of the constructs were performed by assessing rheological, mechanical properties, and analyzing live-dead assay measurements.

summary_en.motivation: To design a self-contained bioprinter that maintains controlled environmental conditions for cardiovascular tissue engineering.
summary_en.method: A syringe-based extrusion system with multiple nozzles was used to print alginate-gelatin hydrogels mixed with fibrinogen and human endothelial cells.
summary_en.result: The bioprinted constructs exhibited preserved cell viability and functionality, and vasculature was successfully incorporated via sacrificial printing.
summary_en.validation: Rheological, mechanical testing, and live-dead assay measurements were performed.

papers.title: Development and optimization of carbide particle-reinforced titanium alloy matrix nanocomposites by selective laser melting

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM制备碳化物增强钛合金纳米复合材料，但未涉及生物医学植入物的应力遮挡、疲劳或骨整合性能。
llm.why_not_core: No porous structures for stiffness matching, no fatigue testing, no surface roughness or osseointegration assessment, and no biomedical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决纳米复合材料中增强颗粒团聚的问题，探索SLM制备Ti64基纳米复合材料。
summary_zh.method: 通过SLM制备不同含量WC和Mo2C纳米颗粒增强的Ti64复合材料。
summary_zh.result: WC/Ti64抗拉强度提升20.88%，Mo2C/Ti64显微硬度提升22.64%，但断裂韧性下降。
summary_zh.validation: 拉伸、硬度、断裂韧性和接触角测试验证力学与润湿性能。

summary_en.motivation: To overcome nanoparticle agglomeration in conventional processing by using selective laser melting to fabricate homogeneous Ti-6Al-4V matrix nanocomposites with improved mechanical properties.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V alloy powder was mixed with nano-sized WC or Mo2C particles (1-3 wt.%) and processed by SLM to produce nearly full-density nanocomposites.
summary_en.result: WC/Ti64 composites achieved up to 20.88% higher tensile strength, while Mo2C/Ti64 composites showed up to 22.64% higher microhardness, albeit with reduced ductility and fracture toughness.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical characterization including tensile testing, microhardness, fracture toughness, and water contact angle measurements were performed.

papers.title: Bone Immune Response to Materials, Part II: Copper and Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) Compared to Titanium at 10 and 28 Days in Rabbit Tibia.
papers.abstract: Osseointegration is likely the result of an immunologically driven bone reaction to materials such as titanium. Osseointegration has resulted in the clinical possibility to anchor oral implants in jaw bone tissue. However, the mechanisms behind bony anchorage are not fully understood and complications over a longer period of time have been reported. The current study aims at exploring possible differences between copper (Cu) and polyetheretherketone (PEEK) materials that do not osseointegrate, with osseointegrating cp titanium as control. The implants were placed in rabbit tibia and selected immune markers were evaluated at 10 and 28 days of follow-up. Cu and PEEK demonstrated at both time points a higher immune activation than cp titanium. Cu demonstrated distance osteogenesis due to a maintained proinflammatory environment over time, and PEEK failed to osseointegrate due to an immunologically defined preferential adipose tissue formation on its surface. The here presented results suggest the description of two different mechanisms for failed osseointegration, both of which are correlated to the immune system.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the immunological differences in osseointegration between non-integrating materials (copper and PEEK) and titanium.
summary_en.method: Implants were placed in rabbit tibiae, and immune markers were evaluated at 10 and 28 days.
summary_en.result: Copper and PEEK induced higher immune activation than titanium; copper promoted distance osteogenesis, while PEEK led to adipose tissue formation.
summary_en.validation: In vivo animal study with histological and immune marker analysis.
